name: Lurasidone
short: D4 and 5HT7 most potent; low metabolic risk; preferred for bipolar depression.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with a relatively simple profile: most potent at **D4** and **5HT7**, high 5HT2A, moderate **5HT1A** and **α2**, minimal **H1 and M1** (Figure 5-53). These may explain its antidepressant profile.
uses: **Bipolar depression** (10+): highly effective and a preferred agent

sideEffects.e: Low weight gain and metabolic risk
Motor effects and sedation (less if dosed at night)

pearls: **NRX101** (Cyclurad) adds D-cycloserine for acute suicidality and bipolar depression (early positive findings)

facts.text: Synergy among several potential antidepressant properties with good tolerability makes it one of the preferred bipolar-depression agents where approved.

Table 7-1: approved for **bipolar depression**; never tested in mania. The only agent with a large randomized trial in **unipolar depression with mixed features**; used at lower doses than for psychosis.

name: Lumateperone
short: Very potent 5HT2A, modest D2, SERT binding and possible presynaptic D2 partial agonism.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with very high **5HT2A** affinity, moderate **D2, D1, α1** and **SERT** affinity, and low H1 (Figure 5-54). The **widest 5HT2A–D2 separation** may explain antipsychotic action at **low D2 occupancy**. Preclinical evidence suggests **presynaptic D2 partial agonism** with postsynaptic antagonism, turning down dopamine synthesis (Figure 5-55).

targets.note: Postsynaptic antagonist; possibly presynaptic partial agonist (preclinical)

uses: Bipolar depression trials promising at publication

sideEffects.e: Little or no weight gain or metabolic disturbance
Little or no DIP or akathisia

facts.text: SERT binding suggests antidepressant potential; if presynaptic D2 agonism is proven, less postsynaptic blockade would be needed for an antipsychotic effect.

updates.title: Depression indications
updates.text: Approved for bipolar I and II depression (monotherapy and adjunct to lithium or valproate) in December 2021 and as an adjunct for major depressive disorder in November 2025.

name: Sertindole
short: 5HT2A/D2 antagonist withdrawn and reintroduced over QTc concerns.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with potent **α1** antagonism that may account for some side effects (Figure 5-60).
uses: Second-line agent in some countries, with close cardiac and drug-interaction monitoring

sideEffects.via: Cardiac safety concerns led to withdrawal

facts.text: Originally approved in some European countries, then withdrawn for cardiac/QTc testing and reintroduced as a second-line agent.

name: Perospirone
short: 5HT2A/D2 antagonist with 5HT1A partial agonism, used in Asia.
mechanism: A **5HT2A and D2** antagonist with **5HT1A** partial agonist actions that may contribute to efficacy or tolerability (Figure 5-61).
uses: Schizophrenia (Asia); more experience in schizophrenia than mania

facts.text: Usually given three times a day; its potential for weight gain, dyslipidemia, insulin resistance and diabetes is not well investigated.

name: Blonanserin
nbn: Dopamine D2/D3 and serotonin 5HT2A receptor antagonist
short: 5HT2A/D2 antagonist with higher D3 affinity than dopamine, used in Asia.
mechanism: A **5HT2A/D2 antagonist** with high **D3** affinity, higher than dopamine’s own (like cariprazine), suggesting possible use for negative symptoms and bipolar depression (Figure 5-62).

facts.text: Its D3 potency suggests utility for negative symptoms and bipolar depression, not yet well studied.
With cariprazine, one of only two agents whose **D3 affinity** is orders of magnitude higher than dopamine’s (Figure 7-72).

name: Aripiprazole
nbn: Dopamine D2 and serotonin 5HT1A receptor partial agonist
short: The original D2/5HT1A partial agonist: low motor effects except akathisia; lowers prolactin.
mechanism: A **D2 partial agonist** close to the antagonist end of the spectrum, with **5HT1A** partial agonism (higher affinity than its moderate **5HT2A** antagonism), plus **5HT7** and **5HT2C** antagonism (Figure 5-56). It lacks muscarinic and H1 actions associated with sedation, and the actions associated with metabolic risk.
uses: **Adjunct to SSRIs/SNRIs in major depression**: its main US use

sideEffects.via: Lactotrophs read it as an agonist

sideEffects.e: Not generally sedating; little or no weight gain (some in children)

pearls: Oral, liquid, orally disintegrating; **4-week** and **4- to 8-week** long-acting injections (the latter with a day-1 loading injection)

facts.text: The result of “throwing a dart” closer to the antagonist end after OPC4392 and bifeprunox were too agonistic; some question its efficacy in the most severe psychosis (never proven).
5HT1A partial agonism and 5HT2C/5HT7 antagonism at low doses are theoretical antidepressant mechanisms.

Table 7-1: approved for **bipolar mania** and **maintenance** and as an **adjunct for MDD**; one of the most prescribed augmenters in the US; **5HT1A partial agonism** (plus D3, 5HT7, 5HT2C, α2) may explain antidepressant action; some **akathisia**; not approved for bipolar depression.
Used cautiously **off-label** for agitation/psychosis in dementia despite the boxed warning for stroke and death.
Gambling has been observed after dopamine agonists and **partial agonists**.

name: Brexpiprazole
short: Aripiprazole relative with more potent 5HT1A, 5HT2A and α1 action; approved later for Alzheimer agitation.
mechanism: A **D2 partial agonist** related to aripiprazole but with relatively more potent **5HT2A** antagonism, **5HT1A** partial agonism (its most potent action) and **α1** antagonism versus D2 (Figure 5-57), which should theoretically reduce motor effects and akathisia. Higher α1 and α2 binding than aripiprazole may add antidepressant actions; α1 actions may help explain efficacy in **agitation in dementia**.

facts.text: Chapter 4 notes that **treatments for agitation in dementia are evolving separately** from those for psychosis in dementia and in schizophrenia.
Positive results for agitation in dementia suggest it may have a satisfactory risk:benefit profile; a positive study with sertraline in PTSD was a promising exception among anxiety/PTSD uses.

Table 7-1: approved as an **adjunct for MDD** only. Stronger 5HT2A, 5HT1A and **α1** binding than aripiprazole (possibly less akathisia); α1 + 5HT2A synergy may aid antidepressant action and evidence in Alzheimer agitation and PTSD.
In testing with **sertraline** for PTSD at publication, with promising initial findings.
For AD agitation: **D2 and 5HT1A partial agonism**, **5HT2A** antagonism and **α1/α2C** antagonism act synergistically on the agitation network; lower doses than for schizophrenia.

updates.title: Approved for Alzheimer agitation
updates.text: Approved by the FDA for **agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer disease**, the first drug approved for this indication in the US.

updates.title: PTSD application not approved
updates.text: The supplemental application for brexpiprazole with sertraline in adults with PTSD received an FDA complete response letter in September 2025.

nbn: Dopamine D2 and serotonin 5HT1A receptor partial agonist
uses: Positive late-stage studies in **agitation in dementia** (approved 2023, see update)

sideEffects.e: Some akathisia (perhaps less than aripiprazole; not proven head to head)

name: Cariprazine
nbn: Dopamine D2 and serotonin 5HT1A receptor partial agonist
short: D2/5HT1A partial agonist whose most potent action is D3 partial agonism.
mechanism: A **D2/5HT1A partial agonist** whose most potent binding is **D3 partial agonism**, with higher D3 affinity than dopamine itself; also potent **5HT2B**, α1 and α2A, with weaker **5HT2A** and H1 (Figure 5-58). D3 action may block limbic D3 receptors and, at VTA somatodendritic D3 receptors, raise prefrontal dopamine.
uses: Schizophrenia; **superior to a D2/5HT2A antagonist for negative symptoms**
**Bipolar depression** at lower doses; broad efficacy across mixtures of mania and depression

sideEffects.e: Some **akathisia** (reduced by slow titration); low DIP
Very low weight gain or metabolic disturbance

pearls: Two long-lived active metabolites: potential weekly to monthly **“oral depot”**

facts.text: D3 partial agonism shows preclinical promise for cognition, mood, emotion, reward/substance use and negative symptoms.

Table 7-1: approved for **bipolar mania** and **bipolar depression**; evidence in mania with mixed features and depression with mixed features. The most potent **D3** binder: VTA D3 blockade releases DA onto prefrontal D1 receptors.

updates.title: Adjunctive treatment of depression
updates.text: Approved as an adjunct to antidepressants for major depressive disorder in adults in December 2022.

name: Pimavanserin
short: The only proven antipsychotic that does not bind D2; approved for Parkinson’s disease psychosis.
mechanism: A potent **5HT2A antagonist** (sometimes called inverse agonist) with lesser **5HT2C** antagonism and **no D2** binding (Figure 5-59). 5HT2C antagonism might raise dopamine release in depression and negative symptoms. It blocks the overstimulated, upregulated 5HT2A receptors of Parkinson’s disease psychosis without the motor worsening of D2 blockade.
uses: Dementia-related psychosis (late-stage testing at publication; see updates)
Early positive adjunctive results in major depression and negative symptoms

facts.text: The 5HT2A mechanism avoids the D2 blockade that **worsens movement** in Parkinson’s disease and raises **stroke and death** risk in dementia.
The **only** known drug with proven antipsychotic efficacy that lacks D2 antagonist/partial agonist actions; in the low metabolic risk tier.

In dementia psychosis it blocks excitatory **5HT2A** input to surviving glutamate neurons that lost GABA inhibition, normalizing visual cortex (hallucinations) and VTA dopamine (delusions) output. Approved for PD psychosis.

updates.title: Not approved for dementia-related psychosis
updates.text: The FDA issued complete response letters for dementia-related psychosis (April 2021) and for hallucinations and delusions of Alzheimer disease psychosis (August 2022, after a 9–3 advisory committee vote against efficacy). Its US approval remains for Parkinson’s disease psychosis.
updates.source: FDA actions reported April 2021 and August 4, 2022
